focus.note: A phrasal verb is a verb plus a small word, like out or off. The two words together have a new meaning. Choose the verb that fits the small word.

speak.title: Role-play: a phone-free weekend
speak.setup: Work in pairs. Read your card, then have the conversation. Swap roles and do it again.

a.text: You want a phone-free weekend with your friend. You would use a film camera, play CDs and make plans on paper. Explain why you think it will be relaxing, and answer your friend's worries.

b.text: You like the idea a little, but you need your phone for work messages and for getting around. Ask questions, say what worries you, and try to agree a plan that you both like.

phrases: I'd love to try a weekend without my phone.
It'd be nice to talk without any notifications.
But what if my boss needs to reach me?
We could check our messages once a day.
I'm not sure that's a good idea.
Let's give it a go and see what happens.
speak.after: Afterwards, tell the class: did you agree a plan, and would you really do it?
